## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Mahāukkusajātaka* (Ja 486) is a narrative in the Pali Jātaka collection. According to its opening frame (*paccuppannavatthu*), the Buddha recounted the story while dwelling at Jetavana concerning a lay follower named Mittagandhaka [Fausböll 1887]. The past narrative exemplifies the theme of devoted friendship and loving-kindness (*mitta* / *mettā*) among animals who assist, shelter, and make sacrifices to protect one another in times of distress [Sahni 2008].

Computational analysis by DharmaNexus identifies 22 matching segments between the canonical verses and the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (Volume 4) [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language alignments, DharmaNexus detects text-reuse matches between segments of the *Mahāukkusajātaka* and various works preserved in Tibetan, such as the *Bodhisatvāvadānakalpalatā*, Āryaśūra’s *Jātakamālā*, the *Saddharmānusmṛtyupasthānasūtra*, the *Samādhirājasūtra*, and the *Udānavarga*, alongside brief alignments with the Chinese *Madhyama Āgama* [DharmaNexus].
